ev-genghis-khan-proclaimed:coord.reason: Wikidata’s point is that of the Mongol Empire item (Q12557), not the event. The Secret History (§202) places the 1206 assembly at the source of the Onon; ours approximates that. QID removed from the event since it pointed at the polity.
checked: The Secret History of the Mongols, tr. I. de Rachewiltz (2004), §202

ev-mongol-invasion-of-khwarazm:coord.reason: Q431177 has no coordinate of its own; the diff uses a generic ‘Central Asia’ location point in the Aral steppe. Samarkand, Khwarazm’s capital taken in 1220, is a better anchor; the full route is given separately.
checked: Juvaini, History of the World-Conqueror, tr. J. A. Boyle (1958)

ev-toluid-civil-war:coord.reason: Wikidata’s point is a generic Central Asia location. The war was fought over Karakorum, Ariq Böke’s capital, which Kublai starved by cutting grain shipments; Karakorum is the appropriate anchor.
checked: Morris Rossabi, Khubilai Khan: His Life and Times (1988), ch. 3

ev-bibi-khanym-mosque:year.reason: Timur’s historian Sharaf al-Din Yazdi dates the foundation to May 1399, after the Indian campaign; Clavijo saw it nearly finished in 1404. Our year 1399 is the start; endYear 1404 is the completion that Wikidata records.
checked: Ruy González de Clavijo, Embassy to Tamerlane, tr. G. Le Strange (1928)
Lisa Golombek & Donald Wilber, The Timurid Architecture of Iran and Turan (1988)

ev-central-asian-revolt-1916:coord.reason: Wikidata’s point is a generic Central Asia location. The revolt began with the Khujand riot of 4 July 1916 (O.S.), which Khalid and the Chokobaeva–Drieu–Morrison volume treat as its start; Khujand is the right anchor.
checked: Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History (2021)
A. Chokobaeva, C. Drieu & A. Morrison (eds.), The Central Asian Revolt of 1916 (2019)

ev-basmachi-movement:coord.reason: Wikidata’s point is Tashkent, the Soviet seat the Basmachi fought against. The movement’s heartland was the Fergana valley (and later eastern Bukhara), where ours is plotted.
checked: Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History (2021)

ev-tajikistani-civil-war:coord.reason: Wikidata places the war in the Rasht/Gharm valley, one opposition stronghold. The conflict began with the 1992 Dushanbe demonstrations and centred on control of the capital, with fighting also in Kulob and Qurghonteppa; Dushanbe is a reasonable anchor.
checked: Shirin Akiner, Tajikistan: Disintegration or Reconciliation? (2001)

polity-hephthalite:from.reason: Wikidata’s 408 counts the earliest Hunnic arrivals in Bactria. The Hephthalite empire itself emerges in the mid-5th century (Iranica: Hephthalites); c. 450 is the conventional start. Record is confidence low with note.
checked: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Hephthalites (A. D. H. Bivar)
Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia (1990), ch. 6

polity-hephthalite:to.reason: Wikidata’s 670 includes post-imperial Hephthalite principalities. The empire was destroyed by the Turk–Sasanian alliance c. 557–563; c. 560 is the standard date (Iranica, Gol-Zarriun).
checked: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Hephthalites (A. D. H. Bivar)
Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia (1990), ch. 6
